overview: This Senate resolution supports naming February 15 through 22, 2025, as "National FFA Week" and recognizes the National FFA Organization, a youth group founded in 1928 (originally Future Farmers of America) that teaches leadership and career skills through agricultural education in schools. It notes that FFA has more than one million members in over 9,000 chapters. It also marks the 90th anniversary of New Farmers of America, which served Black agriculture students in segregated schools until it merged with FFA in 1965, and the 75th anniversary of the 1950 federal charter for FFA. The resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or funding. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on February 21, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors a long-running program that prepares young people for careers in agriculture and leadership, and recognizes the history of New Farmers of America.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
